description: Prompt suite for measuring MiniMax-H3 text-encoder substitution agreement. 102 video-generation prompts (short concrete subjects, camera language, audio cues, proper nouns, long multi-beat, terse stylistic) plus long-form composites built by joining consecutive prompts with a single space until the tokenization reaches composite_target_tokens, then starting a new one. Verbatim from gate G0b/G0c (scratchpad/minimax_h3_te_small_gate_g0c.md), which measured 111 presentations / 3889 tokens with the MiniMax-H3 tokenizer.

A weathered fisherman in a yellow slicker hauls a net over the gunwale of a small trawler while gulls wheel overhead; the camera pushes in slowly as the boat rolls in heavy swell, spray catching the low morning sun, engine throbbing under the cry of the birds.

Inside a dim workshop cluttered with half-finished clocks, an elderly watchmaker leans over a loupe, tweezers trembling as he seats a tiny gear; the shot holds still, dust hanging in a single beam of window light, the room filled with dozens of ticking mechanisms out of phase.

A young woman steps off a night bus into a rain-slick suburban street, shoulders hunched under a thin jacket; the camera tracks behind her as streetlights strobe across her back, then she stops, turns, and looks directly into the lens as the bus pulls away.

Timelapse of a city square from midday to midnight: crowds compress into streaks, shadows swing across the paving, market stalls fold away, and the square empties until only a single street sweeper remains under sodium lamps.

A wildfire crown-runs through a stand of pines on a ridgeline while a helicopter banks across the frame trailing a water bucket; embers stream sideways in the wind, the roar of combustion mixing with rotor wash.

Two chefs work opposite sides of a stainless steel pass in a crowded kitchen, plating in fast synchronized motions; the handheld camera drifts between them as tickets print, pans clatter, and a voice calls out orders over the extraction fans.

A child in a spacesuit costume walks across a suburban lawn at dusk, helmet reflecting the porch lights of identical houses; the camera cranes up as she raises one arm toward a first visible star and the neighborhood sprinklers all start at once.

Deep underwater, a humpback whale rises through a shaft of blue light with a calf close beneath its fin; the camera tilts up to follow them toward the silvered surface as their song carries through the water.

A packed subway car sways under flickering light; passengers rock in unison, one man asleep against the glass, a busker three cars down playing an accordion that fades in and out as the train takes a long curve.

Autumn leaves spiral down a narrow stone staircase in an old European town while a woman in a long coat climbs against them, one hand on the iron rail; the camera retreats ahead of her, keeping her centered as the light shifts from shadow to late gold.

A mechanic slides out from under a lifted truck on a creeper, wiping her hands on a rag, and squints up into the shop's harsh work lights; compressor hisses, a radio plays classic rock, and someone off-screen drops a wrench.
Slow aerial push over a flooded rice terrace at sunrise, the water mirroring pink cloud; a farmer and a water buffalo move as one small dark shape along a bund, and mist peels off the valley below.

A conductor raises a baton before a full orchestra; the camera arcs behind the strings as the downbeat lands and the entire ensemble enters together, bows moving in a single sweep, the hall's reverb blooming.
In a laundromat at 3 a.m. a man watches a single dryer tumble; the fluorescent tubes buzz, a neon sign outside cycles red to blue across his face, and he doesn't move for a long time.
A herd of wild horses breaks into a gallop across a dry lakebed, kicking up a low wall of white dust; the drone flies parallel and slightly ahead, matching their speed, hooves thundering.

An astronaut floats through the cupola of a space station, cheek near the glass, watching the terminator line sweep over the Pacific; equipment fans hum steadily and a radio check crackles from another module.
A street artist finishes a mural on a brick wall in fast timelapse, then the footage returns to real time as she steps back, sets down the can, and traffic passes between her and the finished piece.
Inside a greenhouse thick with condensation, a botanist mists orchids row by row; the camera glides along the bench at flower height, leaves brushing the lens, rain audible on the glass roof above.

A boxer sits alone in a locker room, hands wrapped, head down, breathing hard; muffled crowd noise pulses through the wall, then a knock, and he stands and walks out of frame toward the light of the tunnel.
Dawn breaks over a container port as gantry cranes swing in silhouette; a long lens compresses stacked containers into a wall of color while a ship's horn sounds twice across the water.
